first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down and prior evidence indicates shorter onboarding improves completion, time-to-value, and early adoption; signup simplification also durably improved SMB activation. This directly addresses two current declines without adopting broad promotional pricing, whose prior acquisition lift came with materially worse 30-day retention. Run a standard experiment rather than assume prior effects fully transfer to current conditions, and evaluate qualified conversion and retention alongside completion and activation.

final.rationale: Run a shortened-onboarding experiment. The verified prior result directly addresses the current 4% completion decline and showed completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, supporting sustainable qualified revenue rather than only top-of-funnel growth. Signup simplification also previously improved SMB activation, relevant to the 6% activation decline. Do not use promotional pricing: its verified qualified-revenue lift was coupled with a 12% 30-day-retention decline and failure to survive first renewal. Use a standard experiment to confirm effect size under current conditions while measuring qualified conversion, activation, retention, and revenue quality.
